title: CDL cargo securement practice questions
description: Free CDL cargo securement practice questions on 49 CFR 393 Subpart I. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Under 393.100(a), to which vehicles do the cargo securement rules of Subpart I apply?

options.A: Trucks, truck tractors, semitrailers, full trailers, and pole trailers
options.B: Only vehicles placarded for hazardous materials
options.C: Only flatbed trailers and pole trailers
options.D: Only vehicles that require a Class A CDL

questions.explanation: 393.100(a) states: "The rules in this subpart are applicable to trucks, truck tractors, semitrailers, full trailers, and pole trailers."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.100, Applicability and general requirements of cargo securement standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The rules in this subpart are applicable to trucks, truck tractors, semitrailers, full trailers, and pole trailers.

questions.question: When a commercial motor vehicle transports cargo on public roads, what must its loading, equipment and cargo securement prevent under 393.100(b)?

options.A: Only cargo falling off the rear of the vehicle
options.B: Only damage to the cargo itself
options.C: The cargo leaking, spilling, blowing or falling from the motor vehicle
options.D: Only the vehicle going over its axle weight limits

questions.explanation: The vehicle must be loaded and equipped, and the cargo secured, "to prevent the cargo from leaking, spilling, blowing or falling from the motor vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.100, Applicability and general requirements of cargo securement standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each commercial motor vehicle must, when transporting cargo on public roads, be loaded and equipped, and the cargo secured, in accordance with this subpart to prevent the cargo from leaking, spilling, blowing or falling from the motor vehicle.

questions.question: Which cargo does 393.106(a) leave out of the general requirements for securing articles of cargo?

options.A: Any cargo weighing less than 500 pounds
options.B: Commodities in bulk that lack structure or fixed shape, such as grain or sand, transported in a tank, hopper, box or similar device that forms part of the vehicle's structure
options.C: Logs and metal coils, which follow only their own commodity rules
options.D: Palletized freight carried in an enclosed van

questions.explanation: The section applies to all cargo "except commodities in bulk that lack structure or fixed shape (e.g., liquids, gases, grain, liquid concrete, sand, gravel, aggregates) and are transported in a tank, hopper, box, or similar device that forms part of the structure of a commercial motor vehicle." It also applies to the commodity-specific cargo types.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.106, General requirements for securing articles of cargo (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The rules in this section are applicable to the transportation of all types of articles of cargo, except commodities in bulk that lack structure or fixed shape (e.g., liquids, gases, grain, liquid concrete, sand, gravel, aggregates) and are transported in a tank, hopper, box, or similar device that forms part of the structure of a commercial motor vehicle. The rules in this section apply to the cargo types covered by the commodity-specific rules of § 393.116 through § 393.136.

questions.question: For the breaking strength criterion in 393.102(a)(1), what deceleration in the forward direction does the rule set?
questions.explanation: Forces must not exceed the manufacturer's breaking strength rating under conditions applied separately, the first being "0.8 g deceleration in the forward direction".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.102, Minimum performance criteria for cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: must be designed, installed, and maintained to ensure that the maximum forces acting on the devices or systems do not exceed the manufacturer's breaking strength rating under the following conditions, applied separately: (i) 0.8 g deceleration in the forward direction;

questions.question: For the working load limit criterion in 393.102(a)(2), what acceleration in a lateral direction does the rule set?
questions.explanation: Forces must not exceed the working load limit under conditions applied separately, including "0.25 g acceleration in a lateral direction."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.102, Minimum performance criteria for cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: to ensure that the forces acting on the devices or systems do not exceed the working load limit for the devices under the following conditions, applied separately: (i) 0.435 g deceleration in the forward direction; (ii) 0.5 g acceleration in the rearward direction; and (iii) 0.25 g acceleration in a lateral direction.

questions.question: What minimum downward force does 393.102(b) set for securing an article of cargo that is not fully contained within the structure of the vehicle?

options.A: 20 percent of the article's weight
options.B: 5 percent of the article's weight
options.C: 10 percent of the article's weight
options.D: 15 percent of the article's weight

questions.explanation: "Securement systems must provide a downward force equivalent to at least 20 percent of the weight of the article of cargo if the article is not fully contained within the structure of the vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.102, Minimum performance criteria for cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Securement systems must provide a downward force equivalent to at least 20 percent of the weight of the article of cargo if the article is not fully contained within the structure of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which is one of the options 393.102(c) lists for cargo to be considered to meet the performance requirements of that section?

options.A: The cargo is covered with a tarp that is tied down at each corner
options.B: The vehicle is driven at reduced speed for the whole trip
options.C: The shipper loaded and sealed the trailer
options.D: The cargo is transported in a sided vehicle with walls of adequate strength, with each article in contact with, or sufficiently close to, a wall or other articles so that it cannot shift or tip enough to adversely affect stability or maneuverability

questions.explanation: One option is cargo "Transported in a sided vehicle that has walls of adequate strength, such that each article of cargo within the vehicle is in contact with, or sufficiently close to a wall or other articles, so that it cannot shift or tip to the extent that the vehicle's stability or maneuverability is adversely affected".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.102, Minimum performance criteria for cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Transported in a sided vehicle that has walls of adequate strength, such that each article of cargo within the vehicle is in contact with, or sufficiently close to a wall or other articles, so that it cannot shift or tip to the extent that the vehicle's stability or maneuverability is adversely affected; or

questions.question: What does 393.104(f) say about knots in tiedowns and securing devices?

options.A: Knots are allowed if the working load limit is cut in half
options.B: Knots are allowed in synthetic cordage only
options.C: Tiedowns and securing devices must not contain knots
options.D: Knots are allowed if the driver checks them every 150 miles

questions.explanation: 393.104(f)(1) is direct: "Tiedowns and securing devices must not contain knots."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.104, Standards for cargo securement devices and systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Tiedowns and securing devices must not contain knots.

questions.question: Section 393.112 requires each tiedown to be designed, constructed and maintained so the driver of an in-transit vehicle can tighten it. Which material does the rule say this requirement does not apply to?

options.A: Steel strapping
options.B: Synthetic webbing
options.C: Welded steel chain
options.D: Wire rope

questions.explanation: After the tightening requirement, 393.112 states: "However, this requirement does not apply to the use of steel strapping."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.112, Adjustability of tiedowns (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each tiedown, or its associated connectors, or its attachment mechanisms must be designed, constructed, and maintained so the driver of an in-transit commercial motor vehicle can tighten them. However, this requirement does not apply to the use of steel strapping.

questions.question: What minimum aggregate working load limit does 393.106(d) set for the tiedowns used to secure an article or group of articles against movement?

options.A: One-tenth times the weight of the article or group
options.B: One-half times the weight of the article or group
options.C: One-fifth times the weight of the article or group
options.D: One-third times the weight of the article or group

questions.explanation: "The aggregate working load limit of tiedowns used to secure an article or group of articles against movement must be at least one-half times the weight of the article or group of articles."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.106, General requirements for securing articles of cargo (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The aggregate working load limit of tiedowns used to secure an article or group of articles against movement must be at least one-half times the weight of the article or group of articles.

questions.question: A tiedown goes from an anchor point on the vehicle, over the article of cargo, and attaches to an anchor point on the other side of the vehicle. How much of its working load limit counts toward the aggregate under 393.106(d)?

options.A: One-tenth of its working load limit
options.B: One-quarter of its working load limit
options.C: Its working load limit
options.D: Twice its working load limit

questions.explanation: 393.106(d)(3) counts "The working load limit for each tiedown that goes from an anchor point on the vehicle, through, over, or around the article of cargo, and then attaches to another anchor point on the other side of the vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.106, General requirements for securing articles of cargo (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The working load limit for each tiedown that goes from an anchor point on the vehicle, through, over, or around the article of cargo, and then attaches to another anchor point on the other side of the vehicle.

questions.question: Under 393.108(a), what is the working load limit of a tiedown?

options.A: The highest working load limit of any of its components
options.B: The average of the working load limits of its components
options.C: The sum of the working load limits of all its components
options.D: The lowest working load limit of any of its components (including tensioner), or the working load limit of the anchor points it is attached to, whichever is less

questions.explanation: The WLL "is the lowest working load limit of any of its components (including tensioner), or the working load limit of the anchor points to which it is attached, whichever is less."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.108, Determining the working load limit of a tiedown or the load restraining value of a friction mat (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The working load limit (WLL) of a tiedown, associated connector or attachment mechanism is the lowest working load limit of any of its components (including tensioner), or the working load limit of the anchor points to which it is attached, whichever is less.

questions.question: Welded steel chain is not marked or labeled so its grade or working load limit can be identified. What working load limit does 393.108(d) say it is considered to have?

options.A: That for grade 43 high test chain
options.B: That for grade 70 transport chain
options.C: That for grade 80 alloy chain
options.D: That for grade 30 proof coil chain

questions.explanation: Such chain "shall be considered to have a working load limit equal to that for grade 30 proof coil chain."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.108, Determining the working load limit of a tiedown or the load restraining value of a friction mat (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Welded steel chain which is not marked or labeled to enable identification of its grade or working load limit shall be considered to have a working load limit equal to that for grade 30 proof coil chain.

questions.question: An article 4 feet long that weighs 1,500 pounds is not blocked or positioned to prevent forward movement. What minimum number of tiedowns does 393.110(b) set for it?

options.A: Two
options.B: None, as long as the aggregate working load limit is met
options.C: One
options.D: One, if it is secured with chain

questions.explanation: 393.110(b)(2)(i) requires two tiedowns if the article is "5 feet (1.52 meters) or less in length and more than 1,100 pounds (500 kg) in weight". One tiedown is enough only when the article is both 5 feet or less and 1,100 pounds or less.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.110, Additional requirements for determining the minimum number of tiedowns (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Two tiedowns if the article is: (i) 5 feet (1.52 meters) or less in length and more than 1,100 pounds (500 kg) in weight; or

questions.question: An article 25 feet long is not blocked or positioned to prevent forward movement. What minimum number of tiedowns does 393.110(b)(3) set for it?

options.A: One
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Three

questions.explanation: An article longer than 10 feet needs "Two tiedowns ... and one additional tiedown for every 10 feet (3.04 meters) of article length, or fraction thereof, beyond the first 10 feet". The 15 feet beyond the first 10 feet add two more, for four.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.110, Additional requirements for determining the minimum number of tiedowns (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Two tiedowns if the article is longer than 10 feet (3.04 meters), and one additional tiedown for every 10 feet (3.04 meters) of article length, or fraction thereof, beyond the first 10 feet (3.04 meters) of length.

questions.question: An individual article 15 feet long is blocked against forward movement by a headerboard. What minimum number of tiedowns does 393.110(c) set for it?

options.A: None, because the headerboard blocks it
options.B: One
options.C: Two
options.D: One, if it weighs 1,100 pounds or less

questions.explanation: A blocked article "must be secured by at least one tiedown for every 3.04 meters (10 feet) of article length, or fraction thereof." Fifteen feet is one 10-foot length plus a fraction, so two.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.110, Additional requirements for determining the minimum number of tiedowns (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If an individual article is blocked, braced, or immobilized to prevent movement in the forward direction by a headerboard, bulkhead, other articles which are adequately secured or by an appropriate blocking or immobilization method, it must be secured by at least one tiedown for every 3.04 meters (10 feet) of article length, or fraction thereof.

questions.question: What height does 393.114(b)(1) set for a front end structure?

options.A: 4 feet above the floor of the vehicle or the height at which it blocks forward movement of any article of cargo, whichever is lower
options.B: 2 feet above the floor of the vehicle in all cases
options.C: The height of the cab roof in all cases
options.D: 1 foot above the floor of the vehicle or the height of the cargo, whichever is lower

questions.explanation: "The front end structure must extend either to a height of 4 feet above the floor of the vehicle or to a height at which it blocks forward movement of any item or article of cargo being carried on the vehicle, whichever is lower."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.114, Requirements for front end structures used as part of a cargo securement system (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The front end structure must extend either to a height of 4 feet above the floor of the vehicle or to a height at which it blocks forward movement of any item or article of cargo being carried on the vehicle, whichever is lower.

questions.question: Under 393.114(c)(2), what horizontal forward static load must a front end structure 6 feet in height or higher be capable of withstanding?

options.A: One-tenth (0.1) of the weight of the cargo
options.B: Two-tenths (0.2) of the weight of the cargo
options.C: One-quarter (0.25) of the weight of the cargo
options.D: Four-tenths (0.4) of the weight of the cargo, uniformly distributed over the entire front end structure

questions.explanation: For a structure "6 feet in height or higher", the load is "equal to four-tenths (0.4) of the weight of the articles of cargo being transported on the vehicle uniformly distributed over the entire front end structure."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.114, Requirements for front end structures used as part of a cargo securement system (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For a front end structure 6 feet in height or higher, a horizontal forward static load equal to four-tenths (0.4) of the weight of the articles of cargo being transported on the vehicle uniformly distributed over the entire front end structure.

questions.question: What minimum aggregate working load limit does 393.116(b)(4) set for tiedowns securing a stack of logs on a frame vehicle, or a flatbed equipped with bunks, bolsters or stakes?

options.A: One-twelfth the weight of the stack
options.B: One-sixth the weight of the stack
options.C: One-tenth the weight of the stack
options.D: One-eighth the weight of the stack

questions.explanation: The aggregate working load limit for those tiedowns "must be at least one-sixth the weight of the stack of logs."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.116, Specific securement requirements for logs (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The aggregate working load limit for tiedowns used to secure a stack of logs on a frame vehicle, or a flatbed vehicle equipped with bunks, bolsters, or stakes must be at least one-sixth the weight of the stack of logs.

questions.question: What weight threshold does 393.120(a) set for the metal coil securement rules to apply?

options.A: Coils that individually weigh 20,000 pounds or more
options.B: Coils that individually weigh 10,000 pounds or more
options.C: One or more coils that, individually or grouped together, weigh 5,000 pounds (2268 kg) or more
options.D: Coils that individually weigh 1,100 pounds or more

questions.explanation: The section applies to "one or more metal coils which, individually or grouped together, weigh 2268 kg (5000 pounds) or more." Lighter shipments may be secured under 393.100 through 393.114.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 393.120, Specific securement requirements for metal coils (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The rules in this section apply to the transportation of one or more metal coils which, individually or grouped together, weigh 2268 kg (5000 pounds) or more. Shipments of metal coils that weigh less than 2268 kg (5000 pounds) may be secured in accordance with the provisions of §§ 393.100 through 393.114.
